title: OpenAI prepares invisible text watermarks for ChatGPT and Codex in the EU
friendlyTitle: OpenAI will add hidden marks to some AI writing in the EU
summary: OpenAI says eligible ChatGPT and Codex text in the EU will receive an invisible statistical watermark over the coming weeks, while API customers worldwide can opt in for selected models. Detector access starts with approved researchers, and OpenAI’s own tests show that short, constrained or edited text can be difficult to identify reliably.
friendlySummary: ChatGPT and Codex will soon place an invisible pattern in some text made for EU users. The pattern can help show that OpenAI was involved, but editing or short answers can make it hard to detect.
whyItMatters: EU users and organizations will encounter a new provenance signal, but it cannot establish authorship, ownership, accuracy or how much a person contributed. Anyone assessing AI-written text should treat watermark detection as one clue rather than proof.
friendlyWhyItMatters: The mark may help people understand where text came from. It cannot prove who wrote the final version or whether the information is true.
